text.tspan: Storyboard · Neuri tells us what she feels (left) while we watch her amygdala (right)

svg.text: Neuri: “I just heard Mom scold me: “How could you?!” I jumped! Right now the sound is going
from my ears to my thalamus, the relay station in my brain.”
Neuri: “I'm scared, and I don't even know why yet. A shortcut has already carried the sound
straight into my amygdala, faster than I can understand the words.”
Neuri: “My whole body tenses up. Inside my amygdala, neurons are firing: glutamate jumps
across the synapses and the signal races to the central nucleus.”
Neuri: “My heart is pounding, I can't move... I just want to run away! My amygdala's alarm
told my hypothalamus and brainstem: adrenaline, fast breathing, freeze!”
Neuri: “Wait... it's only words. Mom isn't dangerous. My prefrontal cortex checks the
details and tells my amygdala to calm down. Phew.”
Neuri: “My breathing slows down and I feel calm again. My neurons have settled, but stress
hormones take a while to fade, so I still feel a bit shaky.”
